title: "Palmer Penguins Dashboard: Descriptive and Inferential Statistics"
format: dashboard
jupyter: python3

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
from plotnine import (ggplot, aes, geom_bar, geom_boxplot, geom_histogram,
                      geom_point, geom_abline, labs, theme_minimal, theme,
                      element_text, scale_fill_manual, scale_color_manual)

# ---------- Data ----------
penguins = load_penguins()
penguins["species"] = penguins["species"].astype(str)
penguins["island"] = penguins["island"].astype(str)

clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm"]).copy()
sexdf = penguins.dropna(subset=["sex", "body_mass_g"]).copy()
sexdf["sex"] = sexdf["sex"].astype(str).str.lower()

colors = {"Adelie": "#FF8C00", "Chinstrap": "#7B2CBF", "Gentoo": "#1F77B4"}
base_theme = theme_minimal() + theme(
    plot_title=element_text(size=12, weight="bold"),
    figure_size=(6, 3.6),
)

def p_text(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"

def fmt_p(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"

def decide(p):
    return "Reject H0 (significant)" if p < 0.05 else "Fail to reject H0"

# ---------- Descriptive statistics ----------
desc = (clean.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"]
        .agg(n="count", mean="mean", sd="std", median="median",
             min="min", max="max"))
tcrit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, desc["n"] - 1)
margin = tcrit * desc["sd"] / np.sqrt(desc["n"])
desc["ci_low"] = desc["mean"] - margin
desc["ci_high"] = desc["mean"] + margin
desc = desc.round(1)
desc["n"] = desc["n"].astype(int)
desc.columns = ["n", "Mean", "SD", "Median", "Min", "Max",
                "95% CI low", "95% CI high"]

heavy = desc["Mean"].idxmax()
light = desc["Mean"].idxmin()

mass = clean["body_mass_g"]
mean_all, median_all, sd_all = mass.mean(), mass.median(), mass.std()
skew_all = stats.skew(mass)

# ---------- Inferential statistics ----------
# 1) One-way ANOVA: body mass by species
groups = [x["body_mass_g"].values for _, x in clean.groupby("species")]
f_stat, p_anova = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
df_b, df_w = len(groups) - 1, len(clean) - len(groups)
ss_between = sum(len(x) * (x.mean() - mean_all) ** 2 for x in groups)
ss_total = ((mass - mean_all) ** 2).sum()
eta2 = ss_between / ss_total

# 2) Chi-square test of independence: species x island
ct = pd.crosstab(penguins["species"], penguins["island"])
chi2, p_chi, dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(ct)
cramers_v = np.sqrt(chi2 / (ct.values.sum() * (min(ct.shape) - 1)))

# 3) Pearson correlation + simple regression: flipper length vs body mass
r, p_r = stats.pearsonr(clean["flipper_length_mm"], clean["body_mass_g"])
lr = stats.linregress(clean["flipper_length_mm"], clean["body_mass_g"])

# 4) Welch two-sample t-test: body mass, male vs female
male = sexdf.loc[sexdf["sex"] == "male", "body_mass_g"]
female = sexdf.loc[sexdf["sex"] == "female", "body_mass_g"]
t_stat, p_t = stats.ttest_ind(male, female, equal_var=False)
pooled_sd = np.sqrt((male.var(ddof=1) + female.var(ddof=1)) / 2)
cohen_d = (male.mean() - female.mean()) / pooled_sd

tests = pd.DataFrame({
    "Test": ["One-way ANOVA", "Chi-square independence",
             "Pearson correlation", "Welch t-test"],
    "Question": ["Does mean body mass differ by species?",
                 "Are species and island associated?",
                 "Are flipper length and body mass related?",
                 "Does mean body mass differ by sex?"],
    "Statistic": [f"F({df_b}, {df_w}) = {f_stat:.1f}",
                  f"chi2({dof}) = {chi2:.1f}",
                  f"r = {r:.3f}",
                  f"t = {t_stat:.2f}"],
    "p-value": [fmt_p(p_anova), fmt_p(p_chi), fmt_p(p_r), fmt_p(p_t)],
    "Decision (alpha = 0.05)": [decide(p_anova), decide(p_chi),
                                decide(p_r), decide(p_t)],
}).set_index("Test")
```

### Descriptive Statistics: Body Mass (g) by Species {width=55%}

```{python}
desc
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"**Interpretation:** {heavy} penguins are the heaviest on average ({desc.loc[heavy, 'Mean']:,.0f} g) and {light} are the lightest ({desc.loc[light, 'Mean']:,.0f} g). The 95% confidence intervals show how precisely each species mean is estimated: narrower intervals mean more precise estimates.")
```

### Distribution of Body Mass

```{python}
(
    ggplot(clean, aes(x="body_mass_g", fill="species"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=25, alpha=0.85)
    + scale_fill_manual(values=colors)
    + labs(title="Distribution of Body Mass", x="Body mass (g)",
           y="Number of penguins", fill="Species")
    + base_theme
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"**Interpretation:** Body mass has a mean of {mean_all:,.0f} g, a median of {median_all:,.0f} g, and a standard deviation of {sd_all:,.0f} g (skewness = {skew_all:.2f}). Because the species differ in size, the histogram combines several overlapping groups instead of one bell curve.")
```

## Row {height=29%}

### Body Mass by Species (ANOVA and t-test)

```{python}
(
    ggplot(clean, aes(x="species", y="body_mass_g", fill="species"))
    + geom_boxplot(alpha=0.85)
    + scale_fill_manual(values=colors)
    + labs(title="Body Mass by Species", x="Species",
           y="Body mass (g)", fill="Species")
    + base_theme
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
sig = "a significant" if p_anova < 0.05 else "no significant"
sex_sig = "significantly heavier" if (p_t < 0.05 and male.mean() > female.mean()) else ("significantly lighter" if p_t < 0.05 else "not significantly different in mass from")
print(f"**Interpretation:** A one-way ANOVA shows {sig} difference in mean body mass among species (F({df_b}, {df_w}) = {f_stat:.1f}, {p_text(p_anova)}). Species explains {eta2*100:.1f}% of the variation in body mass (eta-squared = {eta2:.2f}). A Welch t-test finds males ({male.mean():,.0f} g) {sex_sig} females ({female.mean():,.0f} g), {p_text(p_t)}, Cohen's d = {cohen_d:.2f}.")
```

### Flipper Length vs Body Mass (Correlation and Regression)

```{python}
(
    ggplot(clean, aes(x="flipper_length_mm", y="body_mass_g"))
    + geom_point(aes(color="species"), alpha=0.8)
    + geom_abline(intercept=lr.intercept, slope=lr.slope, color="black")
    + scale_color_manual(values=colors)
    + labs(title="Flipper Length vs Body Mass", x="Flipper length (mm)",
           y="Body mass (g)", color="Species")
    + base_theme
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
direction = "positive" if r > 0 else "negative"
print(f"**Interpretation:** There is a {direction} correlation between flipper length and body mass (r = {r:.2f}, {p_text(p_r)}). The regression line (black) suggests each extra millimeter of flipper length is associated with about {lr.slope:,.1f} g more body mass, and flipper length explains {r**2*100:.0f}% of the variation in body mass.")
```

## Row {height=29%}

### Species Across Islands (Chi-square Test)

```{python}
(
    ggplot(penguins, aes(x="island", fill="species"))
    + geom_bar()
    + scale_fill_manual(values=colors)
    + labs(title="Penguin Counts by Island and Species", x="Island",
           y="Number of penguins", fill="Species")
    + base_theme
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
top_island = penguins["island"].value_counts().idxmax()
top_species = penguins["species"].value_counts().idxmax()
assoc = "are associated" if p_chi < 0.05 else "are not significantly associated"
print(f"**Interpretation:** {top_island} has the most penguins ({(penguins['island'] == top_island).sum()}), and {top_species} is the most observed species ({(penguins['species'] == top_species).sum()}). A chi-square test of independence shows species and island {assoc} (chi-square({dof}) = {chi2:.1f}, {p_text(p_chi)}, Cramer's V = {cramers_v:.2f}), meaning species are not spread evenly across the islands.")
```
